column1: # TXV-152 verdicts (9 Oct 2026, verifier session separate from TXP-152; PREREG-txeng2-4 V1; LANE TX-ENGINEER-2): the three positions TXP-152's RESULTS called truth-doubtful. Decided from the decipherment slip pasted on f.151v (harvest/f152r/slip_f151v_c154_1350_750_2350_1050.jpg, native, a later hand than the letter) and the printed 1572 key (harvest/key_1572_sheet.tsv, Tomokiyo; clerk C rows as the build). No cipher sign was read: ref_sign is the committed passC sign, used only for its printed value. Applied by benchmark-tx/build_birago152.py exactly as build_birago87.py applies no.87's: FLAG writes `class` to the flag column (truth unchanged; tx_bench --exclude-flagged drops it); CORRECT re-forces correct_plain through the key (plus add_signs) and writes `corrected:<class>` (still scored). A verdict here replaces the build's automatic align-conflict flag at that position; L03.8 (align-conflict, not in V1) is left as built.

column8: slip L3 "..e.ermi": the letter between the dots has the closed looped head of this hand's e, the same shape as the e of "ermi" and "ione" beside it, not its open c (cf. "incompromesa", "poiche"); NEVBIR-152's "..c.ermi" (slip_for_align.tsv, decipherment_slip.tsv) is a transcription misreading of the slip; printed T86 = e agrees; 4 slip characters on 4 signs (L03.30-33), so the alignment itself is sound

slip L4 "incompromesa": the final a is clearly written (closed bowl, exit stroke); the committed sign T52 is i in the printed key and {i,o} under the clerk C row, never a; the slip's decipherer (later hand, standing in for the clerk) wrote a where the key gives o ("compromesso"); the image supports a, so not correctable from the image, but doubtful as a sign truth; whether the cipher sign is a misread a-sign is not decidable without reading the cipher

slip L4 "la [l]onore": "la" in the line's pale ink, then an inserted raised stroke in darker ink (NEVBIR-152: superscript l) before "onore"; 8 slip letters "lalonore" on 7 signs (L04.17-23), so one letter is the aligner's remainder and the truth l at this sign is its split, not a letter the image forces; the committed T64 is h in the printed key (an "l'honore" spelling the slip does not write), so neither l nor a nor h is forced by the image
